questions.stem: A developer wants to test a Lambda function locally with a realistic Amazon S3 event before deploying. Which AWS SAM CLI steps will do this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Create a sample S3 event payload with sam local generate-event
options.rationale: generate-event writes a sample event in the shape the service sends.

options.text: Run sam deploy, then upload a test object to the bucket to trigger it
options.rationale: This tests in the cloud after deploying, not locally.

options.text: Run sam validate
options.rationale: validate checks the template; it does not run the function.

options.text: Run the function with sam local invoke and pass the event file
options.rationale: sam local invoke runs the function in a local container with the given event.

options.text: Run sam local start-api
options.rationale: start-api serves HTTP endpoints for API events, not S3 events.

questions.explanation: generate-event plus local invoke is the quick local loop for event-driven functions.

questions.stem: A developer wants to call the endpoints of an AWS SAM application from a browser on their laptop, before deploying it. Which command should the developer run?

options.text: sam local start-api
options.rationale: It runs a local HTTP server that invokes the functions behind each API route.

options.text: sam local invoke with an API event
options.rationale: invoke runs one function once with an event; it does not serve HTTP.

options.text: sam deploy --guided
options.rationale: This deploys to AWS rather than running locally.

options.text: sam logs
options.rationale: logs fetches logs from deployed functions.

questions.explanation: The clue is calling endpoints from a browser: sam local start-api runs a local HTTP server in front of the functions. sam local invoke is the nearest distractor, but it runs one function once and does not serve HTTP.

questions.stem: A team defines infrastructure with the AWS CDK. They want unit tests that fail if a stack stops creating an encrypted S3 bucket. What should they use?

options.text: cdk deploy to a test account followed by a check in the console
options.rationale: This is slow, manual and not a unit test.

options.text: Fine-grained assertions from the CDK assertions module
options.rationale: Assertions check that the template contains resources with specific properties.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity in deployed accounts.

options.text: cdk bootstrap
options.rationale: bootstrap prepares an account for deployments; it does not test stacks.

questions.explanation: CDK assertions test the CloudFormation template that a stack synthesizes.

questions.stem: A front-end team needs a working API to build against, but the backend service will not be ready for weeks. The responses can be fixed sample data. What should the developer set up?

options.text: A Lambda proxy integration to an empty function
options.rationale: An empty function returns nothing useful to build against.

options.text: An HTTP proxy integration that points at the unfinished backend service
options.rationale: The backend is not ready to answer requests.

options.text: Mock integrations in API Gateway that return sample responses
options.rationale: Mock integrations return responses from API Gateway without calling a backend.

options.text: A usage plan with a low throttle
options.rationale: Throttling does not produce responses.

questions.explanation: Mock integrations let teams work in parallel and test against stable responses.

questions.stem: A developer is testing a Lambda function behind an API Gateway Lambda proxy integration from the Lambda console. What should the test event contain?

options.text: The raw request body as plain text, without any other fields
options.rationale: Proxy events wrap the body in a larger JSON structure.

options.text: An Amazon S3 event record that contains the request's object key
options.rationale: S3 events have a different structure from API requests.

options.text: A JSON object that lists the function's environment variables and values
options.rationale: Environment variables are configuration, not the event.

options.text: A JSON event in the API Gateway proxy format, with the body as a string
options.rationale: The function receives this structure from API Gateway, so the test should match it.

questions.explanation: Test events should match what the invoking service actually sends; the console offers templates for common services.

questions.stem: A team runs dev, test and prod versions of the same Lambda function. Each environment must point to a specific published version, and promoting a release should not change the ARN that callers use. What should the developer use?

options.text: An alias for each environment that points to a function version
options.rationale: Callers use the alias ARN, and promotion just moves the alias to a new version.

options.text: $LATEST for every environment
options.rationale: $LATEST changes with every update, so environments would not be isolated.

options.text: A copy of the function for each environment, with a new name per release
options.rationale: New names per release change the ARN callers use.

options.text: Different handler names for each environment
options.rationale: The handler names the entry point; it does not version the function.

questions.explanation: Versions are immutable snapshots; aliases are movable pointers to them.

questions.stem: A front-end team that hosts its web app on AWS Amplify wants a temporary, separate preview environment for every pull request so reviewers can try the changes. What should the developer enable?

options.text: A Lambda alias for each pull request
options.rationale: Aliases version Lambda functions, not front-end sites.

options.text: Pull request previews in Amplify Hosting
options.rationale: Amplify builds each pull request into its own preview URL.

options.text: An API Gateway canary release for each pull request
options.rationale: Canaries shift a share of production API traffic.

options.text: An ECR image for each pull request
options.rationale: ECR stores container images, not Amplify front ends.

questions.explanation: Amplify connects to branches and pull requests and deploys each to its own environment.

questions.stem: A developer uses Kiro and wants the agent to automatically update the related unit tests whenever the agent saves changes to a source file. Which Kiro feature should the developer use?

options.text: A steering file that describes the testing rules
options.rationale: Steering files give the agent standing guidance; they do not react to events.

options.text: A spec with a task for updating tests
options.rationale: Specs plan a feature as requirements, design and tasks.

options.text: An agent hook with a File Save trigger
options.rationale: Hooks run an agent action or command automatically on events such as the agent saving a file.

options.text: An MCP server that provides a test runner
options.rationale: MCP servers give the agent extra tools, but they do not run anything automatically when files are saved.

questions.explanation: The clue is "whenever the agent saves": hooks react to workspace events such as File Save. Steering files and specs are the nearest distractors, but they guide or plan the agent's work rather than trigger it.

questions.stem: A team wants its pipeline to catch errors in AWS SAM templates before any deployment is attempted. What should the build stage run?

options.text: sam local start-api against the template
options.rationale: This serves the API locally; it is not a template check.

options.text: sam logs
options.rationale: logs reads logs from deployed functions.

options.text: sam delete
options.rationale: delete removes a deployed stack.

options.text: sam validate, with linting turned on
options.rationale: validate checks the template against the SAM specification and can run cfn-lint for more checks.

questions.explanation: Validating templates early fails the pipeline fast and cheaply.

questions.stem: A team runs unit tests in AWS CodeBuild. It wants each build's pass and fail results, and trends over time, shown in the CodeBuild console instead of reading raw build logs. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a post_build command that prints the results to the build log
options.rationale: The results stay buried in the log, with no report view or trends.

options.text: Add a reports section to the buildspec that points to the result files
options.rationale: The reports section names a report group and the files that CodeBuild reads to create each test report.

options.text: Add an artifacts section that uploads the test result files to an Amazon S3 bucket
options.rationale: Artifacts store build outputs; they do not create test reports or trends.

options.text: Have the tests write result files in a supported format such as JUnit XML
options.rationale: CodeBuild creates reports from result files in formats such as JUnit XML, NUnit XML, TestNG XML and Cucumber JSON.

options.text: Set a CloudWatch Logs retention period on the build logs
options.rationale: Retention controls how long logs are kept, not how results are shown.

questions.explanation: CodeBuild test reports need result files in a supported format and a buildspec reports section that points to them. Uploading the files as artifacts is the nearest distractor: it stores them but creates no report.

questions.stem: Several developers test the same Lambda function from the Lambda console. They want to save test events once and let teammates use the same events. What should they use?

options.text: Shareable test events for the function
options.rationale: Shareable test events are saved so that other users in the account with permission can use them.

options.text: Private test events, copied to each teammate's account by hand
options.rationale: Private events are visible only to the user who created them.

options.text: Environment variables that contain the test payloads
options.rationale: Environment variables configure the function; they are not test events.

options.text: A Lambda layer that stores the JSON test files
options.rationale: Layers add files to the runtime; the console does not read test events from them.

questions.explanation: The Lambda console supports private and shareable test events.

questions.stem: A developer iterates on a Lambda function in an AWS SAM application and tests each change against real AWS services. A full sam deploy takes several minutes each time. How can the developer push code changes to the development stack faster?

options.text: Run sam validate --lint before each deployment
options.rationale: Validation checks the template; it does not speed up deployments.

options.text: Run sam sync --watch against the development stack
options.rationale: sam sync updates code directly through service APIs when possible and watches for changes, instead of a full deployment.

options.text: Run sam local start-api to test every change locally
options.rationale: That runs the code locally, not against the deployed stack and real services.

options.text: Run sam package with a larger S3 bucket
options.rationale: Bucket size does not affect deployment speed.

questions.explanation: sam sync (AWS SAM Accelerate) shortens the feedback loop for testing in the cloud. It is meant for development stacks, not production.

questions.stem: A developer runs sam local invoke for a function that reads a TABLE_NAME environment variable. Locally the variable is empty, so the test fails. How should the developer provide a value for the local test?

options.text: Hardcode the table name in the function for local runs
options.rationale: This changes the code under test and can leak into a deployment.

options.text: Set the variable in the Lambda console for the deployed function
options.rationale: Console settings apply to the deployed function, not to a local invocation.

options.text: Pass a JSON file of environment variable values with --env-vars
options.rationale: The file overrides environment variables for the local invocation.

options.text: Add the value to the event payload passed with --event
options.rationale: The event is the function's input, not its environment.

questions.explanation: sam local invoke and start-api accept --env-vars to set environment variables locally.

questions.stem: A team defines its infrastructure with the AWS CDK. It wants a test that fails whenever the synthesized CloudFormation template changes in any way, so that every change is reviewed on purpose. Which kind of test should the team write?

options.text: A fine-grained assertion that checks one property of one resource
options.rationale: Fine-grained assertions check specific properties and miss changes elsewhere.

options.text: A unit test of the application's Lambda function code
options.rationale: This tests the function, not the infrastructure template.

options.text: An integration test that deploys the stack to production and checks it
options.rationale: Deploying to production is not a way to review template changes first.

options.text: A snapshot test that compares the synthesized template with a stored copy
options.rationale: Snapshot tests flag any difference from the last approved template.

questions.explanation: CDK snapshot tests catch any template change; fine-grained assertions check specific properties.

questions.stem: A container image passes tests in the test environment. The team wants production to run exactly the same image, not a rebuild that could pick up different packages. How should the image be promoted?

options.text: Retag the tested image in Amazon ECR for production
options.rationale: Retagging points the new tag at the same image digest, so nothing is rebuilt.

options.text: Rebuild the image from the same Dockerfile in the production pipeline
options.rationale: A rebuild can produce a different image.

options.text: Use the latest tag in every environment's task definition
options.rationale: latest moves with every push, so production might run an image that was never tested.

options.text: Export the running test container to a file and import it in production
options.rationale: This is a manual process that bypasses the registry and its scanning.

questions.explanation: Promote by image digest or by retagging the tested image, not by rebuilding.

questions.stem: A team wants to test a new deployment of a REST API in Amazon API Gateway with 10 percent of real production traffic before all clients use it. What should the developer configure?

options.text: A new stage named prod2, and ask 10 percent of clients to switch to it
options.rationale: This needs client changes and does not split traffic automatically.

options.text: A canary release on the prod stage with 10 percent of traffic
options.rationale: Canary settings split traffic on a stage between the current and the new deployment.

options.text: A usage plan that throttles the prod stage to 10 percent of its requests
options.rationale: Throttling limits requests; it does not route them to a new deployment.

options.text: Stage variables that pick a backend at random for each request
options.rationale: Stage variables hold fixed values per stage; they do not split traffic.

questions.explanation: API Gateway canary releases test a new deployment with a share of a stage's traffic.

questions.stem: Clients invoke a Lambda function through its live alias. The team wants version 8 to receive 5 percent of live traffic while version 7 keeps the rest, before switching over. What should the developer configure?

options.text: Reserved concurrency on version 8 equal to 5 percent of the total
options.rationale: Concurrency limits do not route traffic between versions.

options.text: A second alias for version 8 that clients pick at random
options.rationale: Clients would have to change their code to split traffic.

options.text: Weighted routing on live: version 7, plus 5 percent to version 8
options.rationale: Alias routing configuration splits invocations between two versions by weight.

options.text: Point live at $LATEST and deploy version 8 code to it
options.rationale: This sends all traffic to the new code at once.

questions.explanation: Weighted aliases shift a percentage of traffic to a new function version.

questions.stem: An AWS CodePipeline pipeline deploys an API to a test stack. The team wants automated integration tests to run against that stack's endpoint before the production stage. Which combination of steps will meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Run the integration tests in the build action, before the test stack is deployed
options.rationale: The endpoint does not exist yet when the build runs.

options.text: Hardcode the production endpoint in the integration test code
options.rationale: The tests must target the test stack, and hardcoding breaks when it changes.

options.text: Pass the test stack's endpoint URL to the test action as a variable
options.rationale: The deploy action's outputs, such as the endpoint, can be passed to later actions.

options.text: Run the integration tests manually after each production deployment
options.rationale: Tests after production do not stop a bad release.

options.text: Add a CodeBuild test action after the test deployment action
options.rationale: A CodeBuild action can run the integration test suite as its own pipeline step.

questions.explanation: Integration tests run as a pipeline action after deploying to a test environment, using that environment's outputs.

questions.stem: A developer wants to check that one Task state in an AWS Step Functions state machine passes the right input to its Lambda function and handles the output correctly, without running the whole workflow. What should the developer use?

options.text: A new execution of the whole state machine with full logging turned on
options.rationale: This runs the entire workflow, which the developer wants to avoid.

options.text: The Lambda console's Test tab with the state's expected input
options.rationale: This tests the function alone, not the state's input and output handling.

options.text: An Amazon EventBridge rule that starts the state machine on a schedule
options.rationale: A schedule runs full executions and does not isolate one state.

options.text: The TestState API, to run that one state with a test input
options.rationale: TestState tests a single state in isolation and shows its input and output processing.

questions.explanation: The Step Functions TestState API tests individual states, including their input and output processing.
